title: Verdier biduality on the coefficient class
statement:
Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $\Fbar$, and let
$\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E$, or $\Qlb$.
Use the constructible coefficient categories of the blueprint and put
$\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$,
$D_{X,\Lambda}=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.
Then $D_{X,\Lambda}$ is an exact contravariant anti-equivalence
of $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, and the evaluation-defined map

$$
K\longrightarrow D_{X,\Lambda}D_{X,\Lambda}K
$$

is a natural isomorphism. At the integral and field stages this is
the whole specified category $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$.

For every integer $d\ge0$ with $\dim X\le d$, at finite
coefficients an input Tor interval $[a,b]$ with integers $a\le b$
gives $[-b-2d,-a]$ for its dual. At integral coefficients the same
assertion holds for the uniform Tor intervals of the finite reductions.
In particular the finite or integral dualizing object has interval
$[-2d,0]$ (uniformly on finite reductions in the integral case).
For nonempty $X$ one may take $d=\dim X$; for empty $X$ one may
take $d=0$. Field objects may be computed from any integral
representative at a finite coefficient field and then localized.

proof.text: At $A=A_{E,n}$, with $n\ge1$ and $\ell\ne p$ fixed by [def-sf-setting], apply [thm-fix-general-biduality] to $Y=X$. It gives the exact contravariant anti-equivalence and the natural isomorphism $\delta_K:K\to D_XD_XK$ on the finite-Tor constructible category. For an integer $d\ge0$ with $\dim X\le d$, [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] applied to the ordinary etale dual $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,a_X^{\times}A)$ gives $[-b-2d,-a]$ from an input interval $[a,b]$. This is the finite-stage dual in the statement: [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] identifies $\nu_X^*a_X^{\times}A$ with $Ra_X^!A$ and identifies internal Hom, evaluation, and its double-dual transpose. The Tor interval is unchanged by this comparison by clauses (i) and (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]. Thus the bound is valid in the etale finite category of [def-sf-setting] and in its pro-etale comparison, with no ambient pro-etale adjoint assumption.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; expanded coefficient-stage assembly

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $A_n=R/(\varpi_E^n)$. For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ the bounded residue reduction $K_1$ has cohomology in some finite interval $[a,b]$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in that same interval, so the uniform finite-Tor subcategory is the whole integral category. Apply [thm-coef-integral-verdier]: its exact anti-equivalence is the ambient internal Hom into the integral dualizing object, its canonical comparisons are $(D_{X,R}K)_n\cong D_{X,n}K_n$, and for any given uniform input interval $[a,b]$ its output reductions have interval $[-b-2d,-a]$. Its statement also says that these comparisons identify the reduction of the actual evaluation-defined $\delta_K$ with $\delta_{K_n}$, and that $\delta_K$ itself is a natural isomorphism. Thus both the domain and the specified double-dual map are exactly those required here.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; expanded coefficient-stage assembly

proof.text: For the finite dualizing-object bound take $K=A_X[0]$ in step 1. It is constructible by [def-sf-setting] and has Tor interval $[0,0]$: for every degree-zero module sheaf $M$, $A_X[0]\otimes_A^L M=M[0]$. Computing internal Hom into a K-injective representative $I$ of $\omega_X$, the map $\mathcal Hom_A(A_X,I)\to I$, $h\mapsto h(1)$, is a degreewise isomorphism, with inverse $x\mapsto(a\mapsto ax)$. Hence $D_X(A_X)=\omega_X$, and step 1 gives $[-2d,0]$. For integral coefficients [prop-coef-integral-dualizing] identifies $\omega_{X,R}$ with the derived-complete tower of $Ra_{X,n}^!A_n$, precisely the value $Ra_{X,R}^!R$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and gives uniform reduction interval $[-2d,0]$. This also identifies the integral dualizing object used in step 2 with the notation of this item.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; expanded coefficient-stage assembly

proof.text: For $E$ coefficients, an object is represented by an integral object $K_R$ in the raw scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Apply [thm-coef-rational-verdier]: its dual is the localization of $D_{X,R}K_R$, its anti-equivalence is exact, and its evaluation and $\delta$ are the rationalizations of the integral maps. By [lem-coef-rational-operations] this dual is $R\mathcal Hom_E(-,\omega_{X,E})$ with $\omega_{X,E}=Ra_{X,E}^!E$, and these identifications preserve evaluation. Therefore the natural isomorphism is the evaluation-defined map in the statement. If $u$ is an isomorphism between two integral representatives after localization, functoriality gives the isomorphism $D(u)$ between their localized duals, so the result can be computed from either representative. By [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], $D^b_{ctf}(X,E)$ is $D^b_c(X,E)$.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph; expanded coefficient-stage assembly

proof.text: For $\Qlb$ coefficients use the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Every object is a pair $(E,K_E)$, and a morphism is represented over a common finite extension. By [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] the functor sends $(E,K_E)$ to $(E,D_{X,E}K_E)$ and is an exact anti-equivalence; its statement identifies it with internal Hom into $Ra_X^!\Qlb$ and explicitly gives descended evaluation and its natural biduality isomorphism. In particular $\delta_{(E,K_E)}$ is represented by $\delta_{K_E}$, and its inverse by $\delta_{K_E}^{-1}$. Their composites are identities already at that finite stage. The scalar-extension comparisons commute with evaluation and $\delta$, so enlarging the common field gives the same maps in the colimit. Step 4 computes $D_{X,E}K_E$ from any integral representative, which proves the last assertion also at $\Qlb$. Finally $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Qlb)=D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
